title: Brijpal @ Brijpal Singh v. State of U.P.
coram: Saral Srivastava, J. and Sudhanshu Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner permitted to represent under Clause 6.14 for instalments.
headnote: A consumer who admitted a bill of Rs. 1,45,166/- and sought instalments, restoration, and non-collection of penalty was relegated to a representation before the Executive Engineer, to be decided in light of Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with an expectation of a sympathetic view for instalment facility.
facts: The petitioner was billed Rs. 1,45,166/- for electricity, admitted the liability, and sought a writ of mandamus directing the Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam authorities at Shahjahanpur to accept the dues in easy instalments, restore a disconnected connection, and not collect penalty for non-payment, on the ground that he could not pay the amount in one go. Counsel for the respondents pointed to Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as providing for instalment payment of electricity dues.

holding_units.holding: Where the consumer admitted a bill of Rs. 1,45,166/- and sought instalments for financial inability to pay in one go, the writ was disposed of by permitting a representation to the Executive Engineer, who shall consider and decide it in light of Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks, and is expected to take a sympathetic view and grant instalment facility.

not_decided.note: Prayed for in the writ; the operative direction is only consideration of a Clause 6.14 representation for instalments.

not_decided.point: Non-collection of penalty for non-payment of dues
